recommendation_summary: Keep llama3.2:3b as the decision model. Do not treat the calibrator as training. On complexity, calibration lowered the Brier score from 0.7668 to 0.5592, so the probabilities are closer to the observed frequencies. On reasoning, calibration lowered the Brier score from 0.7793 to 0.6635, so the probabilities are closer to the observed frequencies. On reasoning, calibrated accuracy (0.4043) is not higher than raw accuracy (0.4681). On context, calibration lowered the Brier score from 0.9587 to 0.765, so the probabilities are closer to the observed frequencies. Every calibrated context prediction on the test split is low. Accuracy can rise because that class is common, while macro-F1 falls because the other classes are never selected. The map adjusted probabilities toward the majority class. It did not learn to read phrases such as 'you just wrote'. The most common complexity mistake is true simple predicted as medium (7 test rows). Add two or three of those boundary cases to the decision prompt as labeled examples. The most common reasoning mistake is true high predicted as medium (14 test rows). On the validation sweep, threshold(s) 0.4, 0.45, 0.5 lead with routing accuracy 0.5208 and fallback rate 0.0. At the deployed 0.55 threshold, validation fallback is 0.6042, and the test fallback rate is 0.5745. That drop is a confidence cutoff, not a change in the Ollama class. Copy the validation-selected threshold into routing/rules.json only after reading the validation sweep. Do not retune it on the test split.
